analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/inference.md, model-registry.md, prefix-cache.md), so there is no executable change or new runtime attack surface. The inference.md units mainly describe the native MiMo V2.6 candidate. They keep text-only complete checkpoints, media as noncacheable and target-only, media memory admission, retained-owner quarantine, and no on-disk payload for in-memory video assets. These statements do not loosen the TB-007 or T-041 posture. The model-registry.md addition (head lines 53-57) says GLM discovery uses bounded headers and non-weight file sizes, not a download receipt, and does not replace catalog/source identity or native pre-allocation validation. It adds no trust claim.

The prefix-cache.md addition (head lines 129-153) is the only item that touches T-041. It documents that for the locally selected EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp, SSD eligibility defaults on (PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel) and binds a full-state store, with DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 as the opt-out. This is consistent with T-041's default-on, per-donation-gated encrypted SSD tier and its single kill switch. It does not change the TTL, HMAC lookup keys, salt scoping or KEK purge.

Open question for the next pass: T-041 enumerates affected_files and detection hints only for the existing tiers, and the new GLM full-state layout 'native-paged-glm5next-full-state-v1' (under libs/mlx-swift-lm/.../Prefix/GLM5Next/) is not listed. Code was not supplied, so I cannot verify that it reuses the DBK3 AES-GCM/HMAC-name/TTL path, the cacheSalt scoping, and the weight-hash binding. This is a verification question, not a finding, because the docs only claim reuse of the encrypted restore path. A threat-model update may be warranted once the code is reviewed.
